speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for National Development regarding the use of live chickens and chicks in an art installation at the National Gallery Singapore (a) whether veterinary expert inputs have been sought prior to the deployment of the chickens; and (b) what is known regarding the impact on the animals' well-being during and after participation in the art installation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: As the exhibition would raise awareness on animal welfare, NParks had also assessed that it would fulfil the licensing condition for public education.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Some of these young Singaporeans felt very concerned, some as young as Primary 5 and Primary 6.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: They shared their views with me, and I raise these views on their behalf.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State if he can confirm exactly what happened to these chickens and chicks after they were made use of for the art installation?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: When was the last check done on the well-being of these animals?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Did they show any evidence of distress or harm thereafter?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Because it has to be a longitudinal follow-up to make sure they are still alright.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can I also ask the Senior Minister of State, given the profile of the venue, NGS, is this a trend of what is going to come?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Because there are some young Singaporeans who are concerned, notwithstanding the educational objectives described, about what message we	are sending when animals are made use of in an art installation in this way.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: These are legitimate views, and I would like to seek the Ministry of National Development's (MND) view on these as well.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I do hope that this is something that they will carry back to the community, to care for the different animals in it.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: On the questions that the Member has raised, let me take them in turn.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: On the first, allow me to reiterate what I said in my earlier reply.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: A licence is required from NParks before an exhibition of live animals can be held.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: As part of the licence application process, NParks does look into the health, safety and welfare of the animals, including the provision of food, rest and housing, before the licence application is approved.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: As part of the licence application, NParks also looks at whether the exhibition has a public education element.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: As I mentioned earlier, our understanding for this art installation was that the animals would be there for a few days and the installation is meant to raise awareness on animal welfare and the need to care for and to live with the animals in our community.
